data_notice: Independently curated linguistic facts and brief forms, attributed to the primary sources; conservatively preserve CC-BY-SA-4.0 notice. No book pages or recordings are redistributed.
limits: No acoustic carrier, source embedding, selected-profile projection, Windows/NVDA or native-listener acceptance in this frontend-only work.
No ordinary alphabet names, symbol names, numeric grammar or abbreviation expansion established.
Acute/offglide/dot/hyphen syntax is explicit research annotation, not silently asserted to be ordinary Hiri Motu spelling.
Uncurated vowel grouping, morpheme boundaries and written-l realization remain unresolved and cannot be rendered.
Lexical stress facts do not by themselves establish all adjacent-vowel syllabifications.
reference_pronunciation: Bounded research reading of the 1974 course with selected Central-type segment distinctions; this is not a claim of a universal Hiri Motu standard or of all dialects.

rules.fact: Plain voiceless p/t/k retain an explicit unaspirated requirement.
Written gw is represented as one labialised voiced velar stop gʷ; do not silently substitute ordinary g or a neighbouring-language kw.
Lexical stress is not generally predictable. Use exact curated forms or caller-supplied acute marks; do not apply a universal penultimate default.
The source explicitly contrasts táu with one syllable and niú with two. These lexical grouping facts do not license a universal vowel-grouping rule.
Preserve vowel sequences across actual morpheme boundaries. The source identifies ha-orea; no blanket ae→ai, ao→au or oe→oi replacement is permitted.
Exact námo/namóna/namódia and néga/negána/negádia stress forms are independent entries; no guessed general suffix rule.
The course says written lao and lau sound the same; retain this exact lexical segment correspondence without converting arbitrary ao sequences.
Selected course realization uses written v as voiced bilabial friction β and r as a single flap ɾ. Genuine w and other dialect variants remain documented, not automatically mixed.
The course singles out lau and dala with actual l; arbitrary written l cannot be assigned a flap or lateral with certainty.
Keep h in the selected conservative realization; the source also reports real intervocalic deletion, which is not automatically imposed.
Do not import Motu plural stress shifts: Hiri Motu hahíne and kekéni retain the same stress across number.
